```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use Salesforce's existing user accounts and permissions in a Shiny app.
`oauth_db_salesforce_api()` queries CRM objects with SOQL.
`oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api()` queries Data Cloud, now called
Data 360, with SQL. Both use the signed-in visitor's Salesforce access
token and return data frames or native API results.

## Register the Shiny app

Create an **External Client App** in Salesforce Setup. Salesforce recommends
these for new integrations; existing Connected Apps can still be used.
Enable the authorization-code flow, PKCE, and the following OAuth scopes:

| Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `openid` and `profile` | Identify the visitor through OpenID Connect |
| `api` | Query Salesforce APIs with the visitor's permissions |
| `refresh_token` | Renew access without another browser sign-in |
| `cdp_query_api` | Run Data Cloud SQL; omit for a CRM-only app |

Register the exact callback URI used by Shiny, for example
`http://localhost:8100`. For a hosted app, use its HTTPS URL. Configure the
client-secret requirement to match your registration and deployment. The
example uses a confidential server app with a client secret.

In the app's OAuth security settings, enable **Issue JSON Web Token (JWT)-based
access tokens for named users**. Legacy opaque Salesforce tokens can contain
`!`, which shinyOAuth's bearer-token validation rejects. JWT-based access
tokens are supported for Salesforce REST APIs, including the endpoints used
here. This setting controls the access-token format; browser sign-in still
uses the authorization-code flow with PKCE. See Salesforce's
[JWT access-token configuration](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.jwt_eca_configuration.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

Users need API access and permission to use the client app. CRM object,
field and record access still comes from Salesforce. Data Cloud also needs
the relevant license, query permissions, and access to the chosen data space.
Requesting an OAuth scope does not grant those permissions.

See Salesforce's [OAuth registration guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/apexcode/intro_oauth_and_connected_apps.htm)
and [OAuth scope definitions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.mobile_sdk.meta/pages/oauth_scope_parameter_values.htm).

## Collect the settings

Save your settings in `.Renviron` and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-consumer-key
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-consumer-secret
OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL=https://example.my.salesforce.com
OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL=https://example.my.salesforce.com
```

Replace `example` with your Salesforce My Domain. `LOGIN_URL` is the
authorization server. It can also be `https://login.salesforce.com`, or
`https://test.salesforce.com` for a sandbox. `INSTANCE_URL` is the trusted
Salesforce org origin for API calls, without a path. Use the org's My Domain
API URL rather than its Lightning UI URL. A login origin and an API origin
can differ.

The client discovers OpenID Connect settings at startup, validates signed
ID tokens and uses PKCE. shinyOAuth handles acquisition and renewal.
Supply `provider` or `scopes` to replace the sign-in defaults.

## A complete app

The app queries when the visitor clicks **Run query**. Replace the Data
Cloud object and field names with ones available in your data space.

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_salesforce_client(
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  login_url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_LOGIN_URL", "https://login.salesforce.com"),
  data_cloud = TRUE
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    selectInput("source", "Query source", c("CRM", "Data Cloud")),
    actionButton("query", "Run query"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth", client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  instance_url <- Sys.getenv(
    "OAUTHDB_SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL", "https://example.my.salesforce.com"
  )
  crm <- oauth_db_salesforce_api(auth$connection, instance_url)
  cloud <- oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api(auth$connection, instance_url)

  rows <- eventReactive(input$query, {
    connection <- req(auth$connection())
    scopes <- if (input$source == "CRM") "api" else c("api", "cdp_query_api")
    data <- if (input$source == "CRM") {
      crm$query("SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 20")
    } else {
      cloud$query("SELECT ssot__Id__c FROM ssot__Individual__dlm LIMIT 20")
    }
    list(connection = connection, scopes = scopes, data = data)
  })
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- req(auth$connection())
    saved <- rows()
    req(identical(saved$connection, connection))
    req(connection$has_scopes(saved$scopes))
    saved$data
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)
```

Open `http://localhost:8100` in a regular browser. Embedded IDE viewers
cannot complete OAuth redirects. For CRM only, set `data_cloud = FALSE`
and omit the Data Cloud helper and query choice.

The app hides saved results after sign-out, account replacement or loss of
required scopes. See [Getting started](getting-started.html#save-query-results)
when adding other result caches.

## Query CRM objects

`$query()` follows query locators until all result pages have been fetched.
`include_deleted = TRUE` uses QueryAll, which can include deleted and
archived records under Salesforce's permissions and retention rules.

```{r crm-query}
crm$query("SELECT Id, Name, Parent.Name FROM Account LIMIT 20")
crm$query("SELECT Id, IsDeleted FROM Account LIMIT 20", include_deleted = TRUE)
crm$objects()
crm$describe("Account")

count <- crm$query("SELECT COUNT() FROM Account", raw = TRUE)
count$totalSize
```

Data frames omit top-level `attributes` metadata. Relationship objects and
child-query results stay in list columns. Missing scalar values become
`NA`; empty results have no field metadata. Use `$describe()` for field
definitions. Raw queries return combined native `records`, `totalSize`,
and a completed `done` flag. Ordinary JSON numbers become R numeric
values; large integers remain strings.

SOQL is supplied as written. The helper does not interpolate parameters,
create DBI connections, or implement CRM record mutations. See Salesforce's
[Query resource](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/dome-query.html)
and [Query More Results](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/resources-query-more-results.html).

## Query Data Cloud with bound parameters

The client uses Query Connect API on the Salesforce org:
`/services/data/v64.0/ssot/query-sql`. Salesforce recommends this API over
legacy Query V1/V2. Its Salesforce-token authentication lets CRM and Data
Cloud share one sign-in. It does not require a Direct API token exchange.

Specify a data space with `dataspace = "reporting"` when creating the client.
`api_version` can select another supported version, at least `64.0`.

```{r cloud-query}
cloud$query(
  "SELECT ssot__Id__c FROM ssot__Individual__dlm WHERE CreatedDate__c >= :since LIMIT 20",
  parameters = list(
    list(name = "since", type = "date", value = "2026-01-01")
  )
)
```

Each parameter has `name`, `type`, and `value` strings, using the SQL types
accepted by Salesforce. Values are bound separately from SQL. Duplicate
names and incomplete descriptors are rejected locally.

BIGINT and NUMERIC columns remain strings, including numeric JSON values,
so R does not round their digits. Other numeric types become R numeric
values and booleans become logical. Dates and times remain strings;
nested and unknown types remain list columns. Empty results retain their
column names and supported types. `raw = TRUE` returns combined native
rows, metadata, and final status; raw numeric lexemes remain strings.

The client submits once, polls the query ID and fetches remaining rows
with offsets. See the [Query API overview](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/data/data-cloud-query-guide/references/data-cloud-query-api-reference/c360a-api-queryservices-overview.html)
and [Query Connect example](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/data/connectapi/guide/query-use-case.html).

## Token renewal and query lifetime

Clients belong to their creating Shiny session. Each operation pins its
initial authorization and obtains current tokens within it. Sign-out,
account replacement, lost required scopes and session end prevent further
access and discard late responses.

GET requests can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401. SQL submission is
a POST and is never replayed, including after HTTP 401. After a submission
failure, check Salesforce before deciding whether to run it again. All
requests verify HTTPS and refuse redirects. CRM continuation paths must
belong to the configured org and API version.

`timeout` covers submission, polling and result pages. Results are collected
synchronously in R memory. A timeout or sign-out does not cancel a submitted
Data Cloud query, which can keep running on Salesforce. Limit result sizes
in your queries.

Salesforce can omit `expires_in` from its token response. shinyOAuth warns
and applies its configured fallback lifetime. That value is an estimate.
Its `shinyOAuth.default_expires_in` option can be set for the deployment's
session policy. Earlier server rejection can trigger the GET refresh above.
The helpers do not change global settings or maintain another token store.

Errors omit response bodies and tokens. Use `ca_bundle` for a private CA.
Tests use documented response shapes and synthetic authorizations; live
validation still requires a Salesforce registration, licenses and data
permissions for the intended org.
